raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

`render_message` in `encoding_dsv41` and `encoding_dsv32` (and `encoding_dsv4`) needs the index of the last user turn
and computes it itself with `find_last_user_index(messages)` on every call. `_encode_messages_text` /
`encode_messages` call `render_message` once per message, and the scan walks back from the end until it reaches a user
turn. In an agent loop the conversation is one user turn followed by hundreds of tool-call / tool-result turns, and in
dsv41 / dsv32 tool-result-only user turns are skipped by the scan, so it walks back over almost the whole list for every
message: the render is O(n^2) in the number of tool turns.

Rendering is synchronous in `OpenAIServingChat._process_messages`, so this time is spent on the HTTP event loop like
the tokenization in the companion PR.

Render time of `encode_messages(..., thinking_mode="thinking")` for a conversation of one user turn followed by n
tool-call / tool-result pairs (same machine, single process):

| messages | dsv41 before | dsv41 after | dsv32 before | dsv32 after | dsv4 before | dsv4 after |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 502 | 49 ms | 10 ms | 13 ms | 2 ms | 6 ms | 6 ms |
| 2,002 | 658 ms | 40 ms | 194 ms | 7 ms | 23 ms | 22 ms |
| 4,002 | 2,702 ms | 81 ms | 766 ms | 13 ms | 45 ms | 43 ms |

dsv4's scan does not skip tool-result-only user turns, so it stops early and shows no change; it gets the same
signature for consistency across the three encoders.

## Modifications

- `render_message` in `encoding_dsv4.py`, `encoding_dsv41.py` and `encoding_dsv32.py` takes an optional
  `last_user_idx`. When it is `None` (any external caller), it computes it exactly as before.
- The render loops compute `find_last_user_index(full_messages)` once on the same list they render and pass it in.
  `_drop_thinking_messages` / `drop_thinking_messages` are unchanged (one scan each).
- New `test_native_encoder_render.py`:
  - `test_prompt_matches_per_message_lookup`: for each encoder, chat / thinking mode, with and without a follow-up user
    turn, the rendered prompt equals the one rendered with the old per-message lookup.
  - `test_last_user_lookup_is_not_per_message`: rendering 300 tool turns calls `find_last_user_index` at most 4 times
    (it was 602 before this change).

## Accuracy Tests

The prompt string is unchanged by construction (same list, same function, computed once instead of per call), and
pinned by `test_prompt_matches_per_message_lookup`. Additionally checked on 383 randomized `encoding_dsv41`
conversations (tool calls, reasoning, CJK / emoji, partial special-token strings, with and without `drop_thinking`):
identical output.

## Checklist

- [x] `test_native_encoder_render.py`: 2 passed (15 subtests) with the change; `test_last_user_lookup_is_not_per_message`
      fails without it (602 / 602 / 603 lookups).
- [x] `test_serving_chat.py`: 160 passed with this change applied (applied on nightly-dev-20261020-ab580b2e; the diff
      is against main `eb4b167` and applies cleanly).

+"""Rendering a conversation must find the last user turn once, not per message.
+
+``render_message`` in the dsv4 / dsv41 / dsv32 encoders needs the index of the
+last user turn. It used to call ``find_last_user_index(messages)`` itself, and
+that scan walks back over every trailing tool-result turn, so an agent loop
+(one user turn followed by hundreds of tool calls and results) rendered in
+O(n^2): 1,813 messages took 0.55 s, 97% of it in that scan. The encoders now
+compute it once per conversation and pass it in.
+
+These cases pin both halves of that change: the rendered prompt is identical to
+the one rendered with the per-message lookup, and the lookup runs a bounded
+number of times no matter how long the conversation is.
+"""
+
+import json
+import unittest
+from unittest.mock import patch
+
+from sglang.srt.entrypoints.openai import encoding_dsv4, encoding_dsv32, encoding_dsv41
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=5, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+_TOOL = {
+    "type": "function",
+    "function": {
+        "name": "read_file",
+        "description": "Read a file",
+        "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"path": {"type": "string"}}},
+    },
+}
+
+
+def _agent_conversation(tool_turns, follow_up_user=False):
+    """One user turn followed by ``tool_turns`` tool-call / tool-result pairs."""
+    messages = [
+        {"role": "system", "content": "You are a coding agent.", "tools": [_TOOL]},
+        {"role": "user", "content": "Refactor the project."},
+    ]
+    for i in range(tool_turns):
+        messages.append(
+            {
+                "role": "assistant",
+                "content": f"Reading file {i}.",
+                "reasoning_content": f"Need file {i}.",
+                "tool_calls": [
+                    {
+                        "id": f"call_{i}",
+                        "type": "function",
+                        "function": {
+                            "name": "read_file",
+                            "arguments": json.dumps({"path": f"src/f{i}.py"}),
+                        },
+                    }
+                ],
+            }
+        )
+        messages.append(
+            {"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": f"call_{i}", "content": f"print({i})"}
+        )
+    if follow_up_user:
+        messages.append({"role": "assistant", "content": "Done."})
+        messages.append({"role": "user", "content": "Now add tests."})
+    return messages
+
+
+def _encode(module, messages, thinking_mode):
+    return module.encode_messages(messages, thinking_mode=thinking_mode)
+
+
+class TestNativeEncoderRender(CustomTestCase):
+    MODULES = (encoding_dsv4, encoding_dsv41, encoding_dsv32)
+
+    def test_prompt_matches_per_message_lookup(self):
+        for module in self.MODULES:
+            original = module.render_message
+
+            def per_message_lookup(*args, last_user_idx=None, **kwargs):
+                # The old behavior: every call finds the last user turn itself.
+                return original(*args, **kwargs)
+
+            for thinking_mode in ("chat", "thinking"):
+                for follow_up_user in (False, True):
+                    with self.subTest(
+                        module=module.__name__,
+                        thinking_mode=thinking_mode,
+                        follow_up_user=follow_up_user,
+                    ):
+                        messages = _agent_conversation(12, follow_up_user)
+                        with patch.object(module, "render_message", per_message_lookup):
+                            expected = _encode(module, messages, thinking_mode)
+                        self.assertEqual(
+                            _encode(module, messages, thinking_mode), expected
+                        )
+
+    def test_last_user_lookup_is_not_per_message(self):
+        for module in self.MODULES:
+            with self.subTest(module=module.__name__):
+                original = module.find_last_user_index
+                with patch.object(
+                    module, "find_last_user_index", side_effect=original
+                ) as lookup:
+                    _encode(module, _agent_conversation(300), "thinking")
+                # One lookup for the render loop, plus at most the ones the
+                # thinking-drop preprocessing does over the same list.
+                self.assertLessEqual(lookup.call_count, 4)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
